topic: A compilation of bizarre and unsportsmanlike tactics NBA players use to distract opponents during free throws.

hook.first_words: Should this even be allowed in the NBA?
hook.first_frame: A player bending down near an opponent's shoes with a red circle highlight.
hook.on_screen_text_0_3s: SHOULD THIS EVEN BE ALLOWED IN THE NBA? SOME PLAYERS WILL DO ANYTHING

shots.shows: Split-frame video of a player stepping/touching another player's shoe during a free throw lineup with red circle highlight
Free throw situation with players jostling and boxing out early at the line
Luka Doncic wiping sweat all over the basketball before handing it to an opponent or referee
Fred VanVleet talking and gesturing at an official
Fred VanVleet wiping his sweat onto an opposing player's hand
Gary Payton II touching Jordan Poole's ankle/shoe while kneeling during free throws
DeMar DeRozan pulling down his shorts while standing at the free throw line distraction

captions.colours: white with black outline, accented red/yellow highlights

ending.last_frame: DeRozan with lowered shorts looking towards the shooter at the opposite basket.

script: Should this even be allowed in the NBA? Some players will do anything to mess with a free throw shooter. They'll wipe sweat on the ball before handing it over just to break their rhythm. Fred VanVleet took it even further. He wiped sweat on his opponent's hand. And it gets crazier. Players have even pulled their shorts down courtside just to make someone miss.
retention_tricks: Controversial question hook at the start
Red focus circles directing immediate gaze
Escalating progression ('took it even further', 'and it gets crazier')
Rapid clip changes showing distinct funny/shocking incidents
what_makes_it_work: Visual cues like red circles immediately pinpoint the subtle, sneaky antics.
Escalating narrative structure keeps the viewer waiting for the craziest example.
Unusual and hilarious NBA antics trigger strong curiosity and viewer engagement.
